citations.observed: open_binary is a strict object of path, format, architecture, entry_point, provider_id, snapshot_path; no Ghidra project or database parameter
close_binary takes only snapshot_path and overwrite
the analysis-database target kind is selected only by a .hop suffix or an explicit database kind (HOPPER_TARGET_KIND), i.e. Hopper documents
Ghidra provider rejects every non-executable target kind ("Ghidra v1 imports executable targets")
headless invocation always imports the target into project 'rea-project' under the session runtime root
-readOnly -deleteProject: ephemeral import, project deleted at exit
post-scripts ReaGhidraNoReturnFix.java (non-Windows) then the bridge; REA's analysed state differs from a plain analyzeHeadless project
runtime root holds project/, home/, tmp/, cache/, config/, data/, session.json, ownership.json, logs

declared limitations: serves only after default auto-analysis completes; imported Program and temporary project are ephemeral and deleted on close; cancelling a request discards the database and the next query re-imports
session root is TMPDIR unless a path element starts with '.', then /tmp, then nearest dot-free ancestor
the target file is copied into the runtime root and its digest re-checked
startup copies the target snapshot before launch
JVM gets -Duser.home and -Djava.io.tmpdir inside the runtime root
POSIX launches java directly with LaunchSupport -vmargs output, not the analyzeHeadless shell; GHIDRA_HEADLESS_JAVA_OPTIONS is therefore not read
heap -Xmx from GHIDRA_HEADLESS_MAXMEM, else GHIDRA_MAXMEM, else 2G
fixed -XX:ParallelGCThreads=2 and -XX:CICompilerCount=2
clears _JAVA_OPTIONS, JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS, JDK_JAVA_OPTIONS, GHIDRA_JAVA_OPTIONS (6.3.0: lines 262-270)
argument builder has no -max-cpu or CPU property option; only OS affinity can bound analysis threads
REA_GHIDRA_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS default 330,000 ms, an absolute deadline for import, analysis, bridge and readiness
timeout must be a positive integer <= 2,147,483,647 ms
REA_MCP_MAX_RESPONSE_BYTES optional response budget
response budget minimum 10 MiB
default budget is the MCP SDK STDIO_DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFER_SIZE (10 MiB per @modelcontextprotocol/server src-Cqbh3MYc.mjs:7159)
HOPPER_TARGET_PATH and HOPPER_TARGET_KIND still configurable; the transport's removal of HOPPER_TARGET_PATH remains relevant
provider starts lazily on the first callTool; operations run through a serial per-Program queue
only requests given timeoutMs have a client deadline; ordinary tool calls pass none
decompileFunction(function, 0, monitor): no per-function decompiler timeout
decompiler options setMaxInstructions(Integer.MAX_VALUE)
bridge shutdown request deadline 10,000 ms
close: fail queued, shutdown request, wait 500 ms, stop owned process, then remove runtime roots; incomplete stop keeps runtime for a later close
runtime and socket roots removed; leftovers reported as ProviderCleanupError
owned POSIX process groups are token-revalidated then sent SIGKILL
owned cleanup waits 1,000 ms (DEFAULT_KILL_GRACE_MS, line 5) and retries once; non-group path SIGTERM, 250 ms, SIGKILL
snapshot holds at most 10,000 query entries
only immutable, non-stateful, non-mutating operations are cacheable
replay returns the stored result for an exact (target, profile, operation, parameters) query id
results with truncated references are never recorded
CLI --snapshot: replay checked before any provider launch
on a snapshot miss the CLI opens the target normally (full import and analysis)
after a successful call the CLI rewrites the snapshot with all entries
MCP mode is exactly one argument 'mcp' or '--mcp' (as used by tools/run_native_analysis.mjs)
